title: Nocturnal Enuresis
diagnosis: Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea with Secondary Nocturnal Enuresis
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with primary or secondary nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting), loud snoring, restless sleep, daytime fatigue, and behavioral issues. Severe OSA causes nocturnal enuresis through: (1) increased intra-abdominal pressure during apnea → increased venous return → ANP/BNP release → increased nocturnal urine production; (2) disrupted sleep architecture → decreased arousal to bladder distention. Polysomnography confirms severe OSA (AHI >30). Treatment: CPAP or adenotonsillectomy if large tonsils/adenoids. Treating the OSA often resolves the enuresis. Do NOT treat enuresis in isolation without evaluating for sleep-disordered breathing.
chief_complaint: Nocturnal enuresis, loud snoring, daytime fatigue
